title: PHP2Shell Weaponized After Japanese Real Estate Extortion
content_md: SOCRadar Threat Research Unit identified an open directory on 96.126.130.81 that exposed the working files of an operator who ran an extortion campaign against Japanese real estate websites and then turned to PHP2Shell , the pair of unauthenticated PHP flaws tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. The server held more than 3,800 files, including a weaponized copy of the PHP2Shell reproducer package , scripts for web shell deployment and lateral movement, beacon logs, ransom pages and data stolen from victims. The ransom pages and contact addresses use the handle kkkkevin777. The campaign focused on Japanese real estate and property-buying websites in October 2026. The intrusion resembled a supply chain attack. After compromising the website of a Japanese real estate services company, the operator used access material found in that environment to reach nearly 20 other sites on the same shared hosting infrastructure and to pull data on their customers. The PHP2Shell tooling only arrived on the server on October 21 , about ten days after this extortion wave, and the files show no link between PHP2Shell and these intrusions.
